lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: measures of center

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: A sample of 5 values is: 12, 15, 18, 20, 25. What is the mean of this data set?

steps: Divide by the number of values: 90 ÷ 5 = 18.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A data set has 5 values: 19, 22, 20, 18, 23. What is the new mean if an outlier of 54 is added to the data set, making 6 values in all?
A data set is: 36, 21, 46, 22, 45, with a mean of 34. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?
Two data sets have means of 76 and 89. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 6. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Sample A: 31, 56, 54, 36, 39, 36. Sample B: 44, 50, 50, 55, 62, 87. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Sample A, with a mean of 42 compared to 58.
Sample B, with a mean of 58 compared to 42.
Sample B, with a mean of 42 compared to 58.
Both samples have the same mean.

items.prompt: Sample A: 53, 29, 47, 56, 27, 48. Sample B: 45, 41, 41, 43, 42, 43. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Both samples have the same range.
Sample A, with a range of 29 compared to 4.
Sample B, with a range of 4 compared to 29.
Sample B, with a range of 29 compared to 4.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 551 visitors to a science museum. She randomly selects 63 of them to survey. What is the population in this situation?
choices: All 551 visitors to a science museum
Only the first 63 visitors to a science museum on a list
The 63 randomly selected visitors to a science museum

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A student posts an online form, and 79 students at Lincoln Middle School choose to respond. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 35 shoppers at a grocery store, 8 preferred a new snack flavor. Based on this sample, about how many of the 280 shoppers at a grocery store would you expect to prefer a new snack flavor?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
